did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jeremiah delivered to the people all the words of the LORD that he had been sent to tell them, and the chapter emphasizes that the message was delivered in full before the people responded to it.
Did you know? Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah, and others rejected Jeremiah’s words and called them lies, even though Jeremiah presented them as the words of the LORD.

Did you know? The opponents did not merely reject the prophecy; they also accused Baruch son of Neriah of inciting Jeremiah to hand the people over to the Chaldeans and send them into exile in Babylon.
Did you know? Johanan, the army commanders, and all the people did not obey the LORD’s command to remain in the land of Judah, explicitly demonstrating disobedience to the instruction given to them.
Did you know? Johanan son of Kareah and the army commanders took with them the remnant of Judah—that is, the people who had returned from various countries to live in the land of Judah.

Did you know? Those who went down to Egypt included men, women, children, the king’s daughters, Jeremiah, and Baruch. The passage also mentions that they were the remnant left by Nebuzaradan with Gedaliah son of Ahikam.
Did you know? The people reached Tahpanhes in Egypt, and the passage explains that they went down to Egypt because they did not obey the voice of the LORD.
Did you know? At Tahpanhes, Jeremiah was commanded to bury large stones in mortar, in the brick pavement near the entrance to Pharaoh’s palace, doing so in the sight of the Jews.
Did you know? The stones Jeremiah buried were intended as a sign that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon would come, set his throne above them, and spread his canopy over them.
Did you know? The prophecy describes three things that would happen to Egypt: some would be handed over to death, some to captivity, and some to the sword.

Did you know? The judgment against Egypt also includes setting fire to the houses of the Egyptian gods and burning them. At the end, it says that Nebuchadnezzar would leave the land of Egypt in peace.

Did you know? The prophecy concludes with the destruction of the pillars of Beth-shemesh in Egypt and the burning of the houses of the Egyptian gods, describing an attack on Egypt’s religious centers as well.
